transcript.text: Here are the execution constraints I confirmed with the execution desk today. The desk has a hard cap of $5,000,000 face value per cycle — and critically, this is a per-cycle maximum, not a per-trade limit. The committee must size the total purchase at exactly $5,000,000 face value, executed over exactly four trading days in a single cycle. Multi-cycle phasing to exceed $5,000,000 total is not permitted. Also important to note: the $5,000,000 cap refers to face value, not purchase cost. So at 82 cents on the dollar, the purchase cost would be approximately $4,100,000, but the face value counting against the cap is $5,000,000. This $5,000,000 face value limit is well below Victor's $6,000,000 remaining single-issuer capacity, so the execution desk's cap becomes the binding constraint on sizing. I have the desk's liquidity note still in my working blotter if anyone needs the full documentation.
